Netflix does not currently pay regular dividends to its shareholders. Instead, it has adopted an equity-based dividend strategy called "dividend equivalent units" (DEUs). This allows investors to receive shares of Netflix stock without actually owning any physical shares, which is seen as more sustainable and less risky than traditional cash dividends.

In exchange for receiving DEUs, investors must agree to lock in their shares at the current price when they redeem them. If Netflix's share price increases or decreases between the time the investor redeems their DEUs and the time they sell them, the investor will either gain or lose money on those transactions.

This approach allows Netflix to distribute profits in a way that aligns with its business model while also providing some financial benefits to its shareholders.
